headline: Seattle Times and Newsday sue OpenAI and Microsoft for infringement
summary: Seattle Times and Newsday are suing OpenAI and Microsoft. They allege copyright infringement for using their journalism as AI training data. The lawsuit claims AI reproduces passages from their reporting without permission.

headline: An Amazon cargo plane crashed at Miami International Airport
summary: An Amazon cargo plane overran the runway at Miami International Airport. The plane crashed into vehicles during landing, causing multiple injuries. The extent of damage and injury seriousness was initially unclear.

headline: Europe has its first commercial orbital rocket
summary: German company Isar Aerospace successfully launched Europe's first commercial orbital rocket. Their previous attempt in March failed after 30 seconds. The two-stage Spectrum rocket reached low Earth orbit from a Norwegian spaceport.

headline: Boox’s tiny Picco e-reader should land in November
summary: Boox is releasing the tiny Picco e-reader in November. It's a competitor to the Xteink X4, with more details now available. Unlike the Xteink, the Picco will lack rear magnets for attachment.

headline: Lanterns Season 1, Episode 4 Review & Recap: "The Weenie"
summary: "Lanterns" Episode 4, titled "The Weenie," received a review. The episode reportedly stumbles, underutilizing key DC characters. Despite flaws, the series' core strengths are said to remain.

headline: [UPDATE] Halloween: The Game Patches Out Sex Minigame — Dev Confirms 'Major Oversight'
summary: "Halloween: The Game" developer IllFonic patched out a sex mini-game. The removal followed a viral gameplay clip. The studio has since issued a statement, calling it a "major oversight."

headline: The Batman Part 2 Goes in 'Another Totally Different Direction,' Robert Pattinson Teases
summary: Robert Pattinson hints at "The Batman Part 2." He suggests it will take a "totally different direction." The sequel aims for a very different take on the DC superhero.

headline: Zach Cregger Says He Feels Like He's 'Running for Office' Trying to Get Skeptical Resident Evil Fans 'Not to Call Me a LARPer'
summary: Director Zach Cregger addresses "Resident Evil" fan skepticism. He feels like he's on an "apology tour" for his adaptation. Cregger is trying to prevent fans from calling him a "LARPer."

headline: Germany's far-right AfD set for big win in eastern state, just short of majority
summary: Germany's far-right AfD is projected for a significant win in Saxony-Anhalt. They are expected to secure 44% of the vote, calling it a "historic result." This places them far ahead of conservatives, who are at 17%.

headline: Five dead after Amazon cargo plane crashes at Miami airport
summary: An Amazon cargo plane crashed at Miami airport. The Boeing 767-300 overran the runway and caught fire. Officials report five dead and five seriously injured.

headline: Protesters block roads in Portsmouth as 140 migrants rescued
summary: Protesters blocked roads in Portsmouth following a migrant rescue. 140 migrants were reportedly rescued in the area. The government condemned the "thuggish behaviour" at the anti-migrant protest.

headline: Chancellor to say UK economy 'turning a corner' despite debt concerns
summary: The UK Chancellor is expected to declare the economy is "turning a corner." This statement comes despite ongoing debt concerns. John Healey will unveil plans for widespread growth ahead of his Budget.
